title: Incident Runbook Template
summary: Master Incident Runbook Template through explanation, prediction, implementation, and review.

challenges.title: Recall checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Without reopening the lesson, explain Incident Runbook Template in your own words. Include the problem it solves, the core mechanism, and one boundary or failure.
challenges.hint: Use “Service and owner” as a cue, then close the lesson again.

challenges.title: Prediction checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Choose one example or source file from this mission. Predict its behavior for a normal input and a changed or invalid input before running or revealing the reference. Explain the rule separating the outcomes.
challenges.hint: Change one condition at a time so the result teaches a rule.

challenges.title: Build and prove checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Implement, debug, or adapt the mission exercise yourself. Record the acceptance criterion, command or interaction used to verify it, failure evidence, and one tradeoff. Do not paste the reference solution.
challenges.hint: A passing check, measured result, focused diff, or reproducible demo is stronger than ‘done.’

files.content:
# Incident Runbook Template

## Service and owner

- Service:
- Repository:
- Dashboard:
- Logs:
- Deployment:
- Data store:

## User impact

Describe the user-visible symptoms and the critical journeys affected.

## First five minutes

1. Confirm impact using an external/user-visible signal.
2. Note the start time and assign an incident lead.
3. Check recent deployments, migrations, and configuration changes.
4. Compare latency, traffic, errors, and saturation with the normal baseline.
5. Preserve request IDs and timestamps for investigation.

## Safe diagnostics

List exact read-only queries or commands and what each answer means. Never put
credentials or destructive repair commands in this section.

## Mitigation options

| Condition | Mitigation | Risk | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bad deployment | Roll back or roll forward | | |
| Database saturation | Reduce expensive work / shed optional load | | |
| Realtime outage | Fall back to explicit refresh/polling | | |
| Worker backlog | Pause producers or scale bounded consumers | | |

## Recovery verification

- Critical synthetic journey succeeds.
- Error rate and latency return to baseline.
- Queued work drains without duplicate effects.
- Data invariants remain true.
- Support/user communication is updated.

## Escalation

Define when and to whom the incident is escalated. For a personal project,
name the point at which you stop experimenting and restore the last known good
version.

## Follow-up

Open corrective issues with owners and due dates. Complete the postmortem
template within two days while the evidence is fresh.
